title: acre-gui clips its render until the window gets input
body:
decade started `acre-gui` as its own window in the scratch pane `terminal3` while a session worked acre-8ed0f4. The document was the default `untitled` one, a 640 by 360 canvas holding one box. Two screenshots of the pane, taken with decade's `screenshot` tool, are kept in `tmp-claude/2026-11-12-decade-scratch/` in the acre checkout. That directory is not in git and lives on one machine only.

- `before-click.png` is the first frame. The render runs off the right edge of the pane. At the scale it was drawn, the canvas would need about 940 pixels, and the pane leaves about 740.
- `after-click.png` was taken after Jack clicked the pane. The canvas fits, at about 730 pixels wide, and nothing else changed in the source.

The window's height also differs between the two. The status bar holding `untitled` sits about 40 pixels higher in the second shot, and a strip of another colour shows below the window. This suggests that acre-gui drew its first frame at a size other than the one decade gave it, and drew again only when the click arrived. Nobody has checked this. The fault could be in acre-gui, in egui's handling of a resize, or in how decade sizes the window it places.

## Open

- Whether acre-gui gets a resize event when decade places it, and whether egui repaints on it.
- Whether the same thing happens when acre-gui starts outside decade.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cd2d1020
notes.text:
The cause is in the compositor, not in acre-gui. A trace of a run inside decade's scratch pane logged every call to `App::logic` and `App::ui`. `logic` ran every 250 to 750 ms, as `request_repaint_after` asks. `ui` ran once, for the first frame, and never again until input. eframe 0.37 calls `ui` only on winit's `RedrawRequested`, which on Wayland waits for the compositor's frame callback. While that callback is withheld, eframe runs `logic` alone (`MISSED_REDRAW_TIMEOUT` and `update_logic_only` in eframe's `src/native/run.rs` and `epi_integration.rs`). So decade sends acre-gui's window no frame callbacks after the first frame, and acre-gui's state moves on while the window shows its first frame.

The same trace showed a reload from disk and the fitted zoom reaching `App`'s state with the window unchanged. acre-gui can do nothing about this short of drawing without frame callbacks. The fix belongs in decade.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/f5ffdd3d
notes.text:
This note's conclusion is wrong. decade answers frame callbacks only after it renders, and it renders only while its viewer window is on screen. Jack had probably switched Hyprland to another workspace during this run. A reproduction in decade-7091e6 froze a viewer for 4 s, and frame callbacks to the panes stopped for the same 4 s. With decade on screen, acre-gui should get its callbacks.

decade-7091e6 now covers a related decade bug. A pane screenshot taken while no viewer is on screen shows a frame the app has not redrawn. That bug explains why the screenshots in this issue showed the first frame. Nobody has explained why the first frame was drawn at the wrong size. That may be a bug of its own.
